items.headline: Medetomidine withdrawal is driving ICU-level care
items.summary: At two Penn hospitals, use of dexmedetomidine among inpatients with opioid use disorder rose from about 6% to about 20% after mid-2024. It reached about 32% in the last quarter they looked at. Hospitalist, ED, and consult teams should plan for alpha-2 withdrawal protocols and ICU beds.

items.headline: EHR nondrug pain pathway cuts opioids after surgery
items.summary: The NOHARM trial tested an EHR-embedded package of patient education, clinician decision support, and self-management tools at six surgical centers. It reduced in-hospital opioid use and opioid prescriptions at discharge. Pain interference, physical function, and safety outcomes did not get worse.

items.headline: One in nine older adults who use cannabis meet criteria for cannabis use disorder
items.summary: A study in Addiction found that 11.4% of U.S. adults 65 and older who used cannabis in the past year met DSM-5 criteria for cannabis use disorder. Most cases were mild, but nearly a quarter were moderate or severe. The authors urge routine cannabis screening in older-adult care.

items.headline: HRSA awards $89.3 million for rural addiction and recovery care
items.summary: HRSA's Rural Communities Opioid Response Program is funding prevention, treatment, and recovery work in 45 states and one territory. This is separate from SAMHSA's $247.9 million announcement earlier this week. Rural clinics should watch for local awardees that add referral, workforce, and overdose-response capacity.

items.headline: More pharmacies stock buprenorphine, but rural ED starts still lag
items.summary: From 2019 to 2025, pharmacy buprenorphine availability rose from 65% to 80% in rural counties and from 65% to 72% in urban counties. Emergency department adoption rose to 31% in urban counties but only 10% in rural ones. Bridge, telehealth, and follow-up pathways still matter where ED starts are rare.
